records.title: DeadTag: re-registered domains of defunct analytics and advertising tags redirect visitors of thousands of sites, among them to a page that serves the Coruna and DarkSword iPhone exploit kits, which compromise a vulnerable device when the page opens
records.headline: DeadTag: expired tag domains send visitors to iPhone exploit kits; opening the page is enough on vulnerable iOS
records.summary: Report URI and iVerify report that an operator they call DeadTag buys the expired domains of old analytics and advertising tags that thousands of websites still load, so every page that carries the tag runs the operator's script, and sells the visitors on; Report URI counts more than 660 re-registered domains. For chosen iPhone visitors one chain ends at a page that serves the Coruna kit to iOS 13 to 17.2.1 and a modified DarkSword kit to iOS 18.4 to 18.7, both of which attack the browser itself, so that opening the page compromises a vulnerable device and steals keychain passwords and crypto-wallet data.
actions: List every third-party script domain on the public websites your organisation, its agencies and its hosting suppliers run, and remove or re-verify each whose provider has shut down, because DeadTag buys exactly those expired domains.

records.title: CVE-2026-48356 (PolyShell), Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source: an unauthenticated file upload attacked since March 2026, fixed for supported lines in July, and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-10-27
records.headline: PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356): Magento upload flaw attacked since March, fixed in July, CISA lists it as exploited
records.summary: Sansec reports that PolyShell, the unauthenticated file upload in the Magento and Adobe Commerce REST API that Adobe tracks as CVE-2026-48356, has been attacked since 2026-03-19, with a mass wave on 2026-03-30 that put a JavaScript loader on 471 stores in one hour. Adobe's bulletin APSB26-73 of 2026-07-14 names the 2026-jul builds as the fix and still says Adobe knows of no exploits, while Sansec says Magento 2.4.9 carried a fix on 2026-05-12; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27. A store that ran an unpatched build may carry a webshell that the update does not remove.
actions: Update every Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce store, those on 2.4.9 included, to the 2026-jul fix in bulletin APSB26-73, then check for compromise: any script file in the custom-options upload directory, administrator accounts nobody created and loader scripts in CMS blocks, because a store that ran an unpatched build since March 2026 may already hold a webshell that the update does not remove.

records.title: CVE-2026-61425 — Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: a client-supplied cookie is accepted as proof of identity, giving anonymous Super User access
records.headline: The Joomla extension disclosure wave adds a cookie-forgery auth bypass — one anonymous request reaches Super User, and Super User means PHP
records.summary: The mySites.guru research campaign against Joomla third-party extensions produced six further disclosures between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-23, and one of them changes technique class: the Balbooa Gridbox page builder (CVE-2026-61425) trusts a client-supplied cookie value as proof of identity, so setting an administrator's username in that cookie authenticates the requester as that user with no password and no existing session. A Joomla Super User can edit templates, which is PHP execution, so this is full site compromise from a single anonymous request. Fixed in Gridbox 2.20.1; the vulnerable code had shipped since October 2025. The same week added unauthenticated SQL injection and order-forgery flaws in EasyStore, an invoice IDOR in Events Booking, and a critical unauthenticated upload in Membership Pro. A follow-up audit of Gridbox produced eleven more CVEs, fixed in 2.20.2, four of them exploited in the wild, and Gridbox 2.20.3.1 (21 September) fixes a further unauthenticated SQL injection present in every earlier build. Gridbox 2.20.4.2 (27 October) fixes two more unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, with no exploitation reported.
actions: Inventory Joomla sites for the Balbooa Gridbox page builder and update every one to 2.20.4.2, which also closes two unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, and the unauthenticated blind SQL injection in the front-end blog author parameter fixed in 2.20.3.1, present in every earlier build, 2.20.3 and 2.20.2.3 included. Anything below 2.20.2 is also exposed to the exploited follow-up batch, which 2.20.1 does not close, and the vulnerable code has shipped since the October 2025 release.

On any site that ran Gridbox 2.20.1 or earlier while internet-reachable, review the Super User list and administrator-group members, remove accounts that entered an admin group through self-registration rather than an explicit administrative action, and review template files and the web root for changes, with particular attention to files written since 27 July.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP (PHP2Shell): two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in the runtime, fixed on 2026-10-21 in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with attack traffic already observed and no upstream release for 8.1 and older (CVSS 4.0 9.2)
records.headline: PHP2Shell: CISA lists both flaws as exploited after honeypot code execution; update the runtime, not the CMS
records.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2), two flaws in the runtime that allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account, most directly on Apache mod_php, with no upstream release for PHP 8.1 and older and a third path, CVE-2026-115560, left unfixed (keep session.upload_progress.enabled=0). CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, after a honeypot operator documented 35 successful code executions on PHP 8.4.26 under single-worker mod_php and VulnCheck extended its working exploit across builds of PHP 8.2 to 8.5; Palo Alto Networks' advisory now reports active exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, SRF links a data theft at TCS Camping's booking-system supplier to the flaws without naming a CVE, and Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to them. As of 2026-10-22 BACS knew of no attack in Switzerland but said federal PHP applications were affected and that it had no complete overview of the update status, and Swiss cantons, universities, Cyon, the Lodur platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution.
actions: Update the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, on every internet-facing server and container image to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or to your distribution's patched package, restart PHP-FPM, Apache and every long-running worker, rebuild images, and confirm the running version, because a distribution backport can keep the old version string; isolate any application that cannot be updated from public networks until it is.

After updating, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 on every PHP host and keep it there until PHP's next regular bugfix release: CVE-2026-115560, which the October releases do not fix, needs session upload progress to be enabled.

records.headline: Microsoft ships out-of-band .NET fixes: hosts updated on 13 October still carry the Windows sockets flaw
records.summary: Microsoft released .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3 out of band on 2026-10-25 to fix the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (CVSS 3.1 8.1, publicly disclosed, rated Exploitation More Likely) and to deliver the corrected fixes for CVE-2026-70197 (Windows sockets memory corruption, CVSS 3.1 8.1) and CVE-2026-102870 (Blazor debugger), which the 2026-10-13 release did not fully address. actions: Install .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14 (11 Release Candidate 3 for the preview) on every host that runs .NET applications, including Windows hosts already updated on 2026-10-13, which still carry CVE-2026-70197; rebuild and republish self-contained applications and rebuild container images from the updated .NET images, because a runtime update on the host does not change a bundled runtime.

records.title: CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)
records.headline: Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now
records.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products.
actions: Update every Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x runtime to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, including the Node binary inside container images (a Dockerfile that pins 24.22.0 keeps the flaw until the pin changes), and upgrade the PyPI Brotli package to 1.2.1 and brotlicffi to 1.2.1.0 wherever either is installed; judge a Node.js build by its release version, because process.versions.brotli reads 1.2.0 on patched builds too, and move any application on an end-of-life Node.js line to a supported release.
Update every Envoy proxy that has the Brotli decompressor configured to v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 or v1.36.12; the advisory names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable.

On every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall on PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 or 11.2 that has TLS decryption enabled, run show system setting brotli and, where it returns Enabled: yes, run set system setting brotli-encoding disable until the hotfix for the release is installed; 12.1.4-h13, 12.1.10-h3 and 11.2.4-h23 are still due, on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30.

Belden says all versions of NetModule NRSW, the router software of the Bern-headquartered NetModule AG, are affected with no patched release and advises disabling the web interface; macmon 6.x and 7.x, Schneider Electric Security Expert and Control Engineering, B&R APROL, HMS Netbiter, Wibu-Systems CodeMeter License Central and Oracle Secure Backup and Solaris 11 carry fixes or remediations at varying stages.
actions: Disable the web interface of every Belden NetModule NRSW router now, after confirming SSH access to it, with the CLI settings http.status=0 and https.status=0, because no patched NRSW release exists; patch macmon 7.x from the service portal and move macmon 6.x to 7.x, and keep the web interfaces of both off networks that are not trusted.

records.title: Gheist: stolen GitHub tokens plant a secret-dumping workflow in every repository they reach; GitHub's July approval hold stops it on public github.com repositories but not on private ones or GitHub Enterprise Server
records.headline: Gheist abuses stolen GitHub tokens to dump secrets through Actions; GitHub's hold covers public repositories only
records.summary: Wiz Research has tracked since 2026-09-15 an automated campaign, Gheist, that uses stolen GitHub tokens to commit a secret-dumping Actions workflow to every repository each token can reach, more than 13,500 branches from more than 850 accounts. GitHub's approval hold of 2026-07-28 stops the workflow on public github.com repositories, but not on private repositories or GitHub Enterprise Server, where Wiz saw the runs complete and the organizations' own workflows assume AWS roles on the attacker branches.
actions: In every GitHub organisation your teams or suppliers administer, private repositories and GitHub Enterprise Server included, search for branches named ci-sync- plus six random characters that add only the workflow file sync-check.yml, and for any workflow run on them; for every hit, rotate all repository, organisation and environment secrets that repository could read and revoke the token that pushed the commit, because deleting the run or the branch does not undo the exposure.

last_update.summary: Huntress's analysis of 2026-10-26 reads the activity as scripted tooling steered by an operator, rates LLM involvement low to medium on its own telemetry, adds a detection for service principals that assign themselves or a sibling a directory role, and notes that Graph reads leave no Entra audit record.

last_development.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence assesses that Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, was responsible for the compromise, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants after an automated password spray from the same network range, and warns that credential changes planted in tenants can persist after the vendor application is remediated. ConnectWise itself says it appears a China state-aligned group was responsible and began restoring services in controlled phases on 2026-10-21.

records.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick): the vendor's Microsoft 365 application credential was used to sign in to customer tenants, with directory-role self-assignments in about 50 tenants and, Huntress reports, added credentials in two
records.headline: ConnectWise SkyKick app credential used in 162+ Microsoft 365 tenants; disabling it does not undo planted access
records.summary: ConnectWise says it identified unauthorized access to application identities of its Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) service; Huntress and Todyl report that from 15 October the app's credential was used to obtain app-only Microsoft Graph tokens in customer Microsoft 365 tenants; Huntress alone confirmed unauthorized sign-ins in 162 tenants by 16 October and saw ConnectWise Cloud Management apps assign themselves directory roles in about 50 tenants and, in two tenants, a scripted Global Administrator self-grant followed by new client secrets planted on apparently random applications. ConnectWise disabled seven application identities and suspended the service on 17 October, but says disabling does not reverse changes already made in a tenant, so every tenant that ever consented a ConnectWise or SkyKick app needs the apps disabled and its application credentials, directory roles and consents reviewed. Microsoft assesses that the China-state aligned actor Storm-0940 is behind it, using the ARTEX agentic-AI framework, and says it attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants; how the credential was obtained and what data was read are not public.
actions: In every Entra tenant you or your MSP administer, disable without deleting the seven ConnectWise application identities that ConnectWise lists by client ID (Cloud Backup is 506e08f9-6e9a-4da4-942b-a099a03644ae; the other six are in ConnectWise's advisory), dormant connections included, and keep them disabled until ConnectWise gives restoration instructions; where Graph activity logs were enabled, review them for these apps until at least 90 minutes after you disabled them, because a token issued before the disable stays valid for up to 90 minutes, and preserve the sign-in and audit logs promptly without delaying containment, because Entra ID Free keeps only 7 days.
In the same tenants list the apps owned by the ConnectWise S-K LLC tenant (3f9cd7a0-127a-4ed4-bf06-2f830d5616b7), and disable each that you do not use or cannot verify as safe.

In the same tenants review every enterprise application and app registration, MSP management and security tools first but none skipped (Huntress saw the secrets planted on apparently random applications, in one tenant on some of the least privileged ones), for client secrets, certificates and federated credentials added since 2026-10-13 and remove any you did not create; also check the directory roles, owners and consent grants held by ConnectWise and SkyKick service principals, Conditional Access exclusions for them, and mailbox forwarding, inbox and transport rules and delegated access, because disabling the vendor applications does not remove access planted through them.

records.title: ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration
records.headline: Microsoft: Storm-0940 runs the ARTEX agent framework at machine speed; Expel adds an Okta self-registration technique
records.summary: Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases. Expel independently saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration, enrol Okta Verify and sign in to applications, and CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the same framework. Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, hospitals and universities among them, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer.
actions: In every Okta org that allows self-service registration, review the accounts created since 2026-10-13 and every Okta Verify enrollment on them, and remove self-created accounts that nobody provisioned.

records.headline: Apple's exploited CoreGraphics zero-day is now fixed for iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPad 7th generation (iOS 18.7.11)
records.summary: Apple's 2026-09-28 updates (iOS and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1, macOS Sequoia 15.8.1) fix CVE-2026-86950, a CoreGraphics out-of-bounds write that can run arbitrary code when a crafted file is processed, and iOS and iPadOS 18.7.11 of 2026-10-26 carry the fix for iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPad 7th generation, which the 26.7.1 notes do not list. Since 2026-09-30 a public proof of concept crashes unpatched devices with a crafted PDF font.
actions: Push iOS and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 through device management now, and iOS and iPadOS 18.7.11 to every iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPad 7th generation, starting with the devices of staff who could be individually targeted; Apple describes the exploitation only on iOS before iOS 27.

records.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, QNAP QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the NAS web components before authentication; fixed builds of 2026-10-23, QVR Surveillance and TVR OS now fixed, Notes Station 3 and QNE (ADRA) still unfixed
records.headline: PHP2Shell hits QNAP NAS before login: QTS, QuTS hero, QVR and TVR OS fixed, Notes Station 3 and QNE still unfixed
records.summary: QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18 says the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2) affect the PHP in the web components of QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud and several QNAP applications and can be triggered before authentication, and fixed builds dated 2026-10-23 are out for QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud. As of 2026-10-27 the table lists QVR Surveillance (ARM32) 3.0.3.1756 and TVR OS 1.0.5 as resolved, Notes Station 3 and QNE (ADRA) have no fix and QNAP says to keep devices off the internet; QNAP has seen scanning and exploitation attempts in the wild but no reports of exploitation targeting its products, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. Synology's advisory fixes its PHP packages (except the end-of-life PHP 7.3), Mail Station and Calendar.
actions: Update every QNAP NAS on QTS, QuTS hero or QuTScloud to the builds of 2026-10-23 (QTS 6.1.0.3656 or 5.2.11.3661, QuTS hero h6.1.0.3656, h6.0.2.3656 or h5.2.11.3661, QuTScloud c5.2.9.3661), every QVR Surveillance (ARM32 models) to 3.0.3.1756 and every TVR OS to 1.0.5, and take any QNAP device running Notes Station 3 or QNE (ADRA) off the internet until QNAP lists a fix.

records.title: Japan's wave of personal-data theft from web systems: JPCERT/CC and NICT describe attackers who decompile the published Android app to find internal APIs, drop JSP web shells as .war files on application servers, and run AI penetration-testing platforms against exposed web applications and WSUS servers
records.headline: JPCERT/CC and NICT: attackers decompile the public app, then call internal APIs; AI platforms scan exposed web apps
records.summary: JPCERT/CC (alert AT-2026-0030, updated 2026-10-23) and NICT describe a wave of personal-data leaks from Japanese web systems in which attackers analyse the published Android app to find API endpoints and keys and then call internal management APIs the app screens never use, place JSP web shells as .war files on application servers behind the public web server, and, per the latest update, run AI penetration-testing platforms (Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, ARTEX) against internet-facing web applications, WSUS servers included. No actor is named, JPCERT/CC says it confirmed AI used to scan for known vulnerabilities and attack through APIs, and Macnica could not confirm AI use.

records.title: Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update: six unauthenticated network CVSS 10.0 rows in Access Manager, SOA Suite, E-Business Suite and JD Edwards, and WebLogic CVSS 9.8 flaws reachable over HTTP and T3/IIOP
records.headline: Oracle's October CPU carries six unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 rows and two WebLogic 9.8 flaws; none is reported exploited
records.summary: Oracle's Critical Patch Update of 2026-10-20 carries 1295 new patches. Its risk matrices list 90 rows (73 distinct CVE ids) scored CVSS 3.1 9.0 or higher that need no authentication over the network, among them six at 10.0 in Access Manager, SOA Suite (three), E-Business Suite Workflow Notification Mailer and JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Orchestrator, and two WebLogic Server flaws at 9.8 reachable over HTTP and over T3 and IIOP. The advisory states no exploitation for any row, and it points to My Oracle Support documents for patch availability.

last_development.summary: A Swiss victim: Republik, a Swiss online magazine, says attackers used the Metabase flaw against its own installation from August until the tool failed on 2026-10-14, retrieved the records of all registered users and reported the incident to the federal data protection commissioner; it had not subscribed to the vendor's security warnings.

records.title: Metabase CVE-2026-72898: an unauthenticated SQL-injection zero-day gave attackers administrator access to BI instances, exploited since at least 2 August, with VenariX counting fifteen downstream victims
records.headline: Metabase Cloud was breached through its own 0-day; self-hosted instances stay vulnerable until manually upgraded
records.summary: Metabase disclosed on 2026-08-06 that its Metabase Cloud platform was attacked through a previously unknown vulnerability in versions 1.58 and above: an unauthenticated attacker injects arbitrary SQL against the application database and obtains administrator access to the instance, from which they can rewrite configuration, steal the stored credentials for every connected database and export the data those connections reach. The only interim workaround the vendor offers is to block the /api/session/reset_password endpoint, which is also where its published attack pattern runs. Cloud instances were patched by the vendor; self-hosted deployments stay vulnerable until manually upgraded to 0.58.24, 0.59.21, 0.60.17, 0.61.11, 0.62.9 or 0.63.5. Laptop maker Framework and form builder Tally confirmed customer data was taken from instances accessed on 2026-08-03. The flaw had no CVE identifier at disclosure; it is now tracked as CVE-2026-72898, which CISA added to its KEV catalog on 2026-08-11. VenariX now tracks fifteen publicly confirmed downstream incidents and ties two of them, at Statista and Dodo Payments, to the Dire Wolf extortion group working against self-hosted instances.
actions: Upgrade every self-hosted Metabase to at least 0.58.24 / 0.59.21 / 0.60.17 / 0.61.11 / 0.62.9 / 0.63.5, then, for any instance that was reachable and unpatched during the exploitation window, revoke all active sessions by clearing the core_session table, delete unrecognised API keys, and rotate the credentials for every connected database and warehouse, not just the Metabase admin credentials, because the upgrade does not invalidate what was already retrieved.

Search Metabase application or reverse-proxy ingress logs across the entire pre-upgrade exposure window for a POST to /api/session/reset_password returning HTTP 400 immediately followed by a GET to /api/user/current returning HTTP 200 from the same source; Metabase states that sequence indicates the instance was likely compromised.

last_update.summary: Adds Mandiant's characterisation of the initial CVE-2026-88772 intrusions as likely state-sponsored (no group named) and its expectation of broad opportunistic exploitation of both flaws; the analysis now says no actor has been named rather than that no attribution exists.

last_development.summary: Rapid7's incident analysis of an early-October NetScaler compromise shows CVE-2026-88771 chained with the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779, with the call-home crash handler running the payload as root after a reboot, followed by persistence that synchronises to the HA peer, internal reconnaissance and exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material; an appliance that was reached needs the configuration secrets rotated as well as the patch.

records.title: CVE-2026-88771 / CVE-2026-88772, Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: unauthenticated pre-auth RCE zero-days exploited before a patch existed (CVSS 4.0 9.5)
records.headline: Two exploited NetScaler zero-days: one in default configuration, one on by default on VPN servers; no workaround
records.summary: Citrix's CTX697096 bulletin (2026-09-27) fixes eight NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, two of which, CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, every default deployment) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow to RCE/DoS, reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the VPN-vServer default), were exploited before any fix existed; CISA added both to KEV and Citrix lists no workaround. Mandiant, GTIG, Unit 42, Zscaler and Rapid7 describe the compromises: web-server-configuration persistence, web shells, and in one intrusion the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779 chained with CVE-2026-88771 so that the crash handler ran the payload as root, followed by exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material. An appliance patched after the bulletin therefore still needs a compromise check and its configuration secrets rotated. SAML-configured appliances need the later builds named for CVE-2026-88779 (14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28) and identity providers 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29 for CVE-2026-107406; CVE-2026-88773 has a public proof of concept with no exploitation seen.
actions: Upgrade every internet-facing NetScaler ADC/Gateway to 14.1-73.37+ (14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.37 FIPS+) or 13.1-64.23+ (13.1-FIPS/NDcPP 13.1-37.279+) now (a SAML-configured appliance needs the later builds named for CVE-2026-88779, and an identity provider 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29); on a 13.1-branch appliance run `show ns variable` first; if it returns any variables, install 13.1-64.24 instead to avoid a known reboot loop. Capture logs, an instance snapshot where the appliance is virtual, a support bundle and a core dump from each exposed appliance BEFORE patching, since the upgrade can remove forensic evidence of prior exploitation.

Run Mandiant's compromise checks, extended by the Unit 42 artifacts described in the update below, Zscaler's (appliance-initiated downloads to unfamiliar addresses, an unexpected executable under /var, a Perl CGI handler added to the web server configuration) and Rapid7's (the setuid bit on /bin/sh, nsaaad crashes followed by Pitboss reboots, an outbound agent polling an external endpoint every 15 seconds), on every NetScaler that was internet-facing and unpatched at any time since early September, patched or not; isolate any hit, check both nodes of an HA pair, halt HA configuration sync until both nodes are validated, and rotate the LDAP and RADIUS bind credentials, SSL private keys and key-encryption material held in the configuration, since Rapid7 saw the configuration and backups staged and exfiltrated.

Find any NetScaler ADC or Gateway still on the end-of-life 12.1 or 13.0 branches and decide isolation or replacement now: they receive no security updates and Citrix has not said whether they are affected.

records.title: HPESBNW05162, HPE Networking (Aruba) AOS-8 and AOS-10 wireless: 72 CVEs fixed in one bulletin, 19 of them unauthenticated and network-reachable at CVSS 9.0 or above, across controllers, gateways and access points
records.headline: HPE's Aruba wireless bulletin fixes 19 unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0+; HPE knows of no public exploit code
records.summary: HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05162 of 2026-10-22 fixes 72 CVEs in AOS-8 and AOS-10 for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways and access points, 33 of them at CVSS 3.1 9.0 or higher and 19 of those reachable over the network without authentication (eight at 10.0). HPE found the flaws through internal research, knows of no public discussion or exploit code, and strongly urges patching; its only workaround is to confine the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated segment behind firewall policy.
actions: Upgrade every HPE Networking (Aruba) Mobility Conductor, Controller, Gateway and access point on AOS-10 or AOS-8 to the fixed build of its train (10.8.1.2, 10.7.2.7, 10.4.1.14, 8.13.3.1 or 8.10.0.24), and until then confine the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated layer 2 segment or VLAN behind firewall policy, as HPE advises.

last_development.summary: Debian fixed the five NGINX flaws in trixie with DSA-6575-1 (1.26.3-3+deb13u10); only bookworm is still marked vulnerable. Trixie users install the update; bookworm keeps the configuration workaround.

records.title: CVE-2026-15176 / CVE-2026-93479 / CVE-2026-97205, NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus: three unauthenticated heap-corruption flaws rated CVSS 4.0 9.2, reachable only in specific configurations and fixed in 1.30.6 and 1.31.7
records.headline: Three configuration-dependent NGINX heap flaws (CVSS 9.2) are fixed in 1.30.6, 1.31.7 and Debian trixie, not bookworm
records.summary: The nginx 1.30.6 (stable) and 1.31.7 (mainline) releases of 2026-10-14 fix five security flaws, three of them heap-corruption bugs that F5 scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and an unauthenticated attacker can reach with crafted HTTP requests, but only on configurations that combine alias with rewrite and $request_filename, use a regex map whose captures are referenced before its output variable, or enable asynchronous file I/O with server-side includes; the other two concern HTTP/3 and TLS session ticket key rotation. F5 says the heap flaws restart the worker, with code execution only where ASLR is disabled or bypassed; no exploitation or public proof of concept is reported, nginx.org rates all five medium, and Debian fixed trixie with DSA-6575-1 while its bookworm package is still marked vulnerable.
actions: Run nginx -T on every internet-facing NGINX reverse proxy, load balancer and ingress and upgrade each one whose configuration uses alias with rewrite and $request_filename, a regex map whose captures are referenced before its output variable, or aio together with ssi, HTTP/3 or TLS session ticket key rotation to nginx 1.30.6 or 1.31.7 (NGINX Plus 37.0.5.1 or 37.1.0.1); where the package comes from Debian trixie, install the DSA-6575-1 update (1.26.3-3+deb13u10); on bookworm, which the tracker still marks vulnerable, apply F5's configuration workaround until the distribution ships a fix.

records.title: TeamUpdraft breach: stolen UpdraftCentral connection keys are used to push backdoor plugins to connected WordPress sites, with no flaw in UpdraftPlus and no CVE; deleting the keys is the fix
records.headline: Stolen UpdraftCentral keys install backdoor plugins on WordPress sites; the plugin update alone does not evict them
records.summary: TeamUpdraft, the vendor of the UpdraftPlus backup plugin, says unauthorised access to teamupdraft.com on 17 and 18 October probably exposed its customer database, including UpdraftCentral connection keys, and Patchstack and Nethemba report an attacker using those keys to install backdoor plugins on connected WordPress sites, which Patchstack's telemetry dates from 2026-10-18 15:32 (it gives no time zone), and that create hidden administrators. It is not a flaw in UpdraftPlus: the plugin obeys commands signed with a valid key, a key exists on many sites that never used the service because connecting a teamupdraft.com account ticks the option by default, and the update disconnects only connections made before 13:07 BST (12:07 UTC) on 18 October, so keys created later that day have to be deleted by hand. TeamUpdraft says the attacker used a compromised key to enter its own site, and Nethemba saw the stolen keys used again on 2026-10-21, after 1.26.13 shipped.
actions: On every WordPress site your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with UpdraftPlus, free or premium, including old municipal, campaign and project sites, check for an UpdraftCentral key (wp option get updraft_central_localkeys, or Settings > UpdraftPlus Backups > Advanced Tools > UpdraftCentral) and delete every key even if nobody remembers using UpdraftCentral, then update to 1.26.13 or 2.26.13 or later; deleting a key stops remote management only, and backups keep working.

On any site where a plugin, must-use plugin or Editor account holding manage_options appears that nobody created, delete the UpdraftCentral key first, then restore the site from a backup taken before 17 October, rotate every administrator and UpdraftCentral password, the teamupdraft.com account password (which UpdraftPlus Premium can leave stored in the site database and its backups) and end all sessions.

records.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0: the PyPI wheels and the official Docker images carried a credential stealer and a dormant remote-code loader that Python starts at every launch, published through the maintainers' own release workflow with stolen developer tokens
records.headline: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI and in the official images stole cloud and AI credentials; removing the package does not stop it
records.summary: On 2026-10-21 LiteLLM 1.107.0, the open-source LLM gateway, shipped with malicious Python startup files in all seven PyPI wheels (live 11:39 to 13:23 UTC) and in the official GHCR and Docker Hub images behind the v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable tags (11:46 to 14:20 UTC); they run a credential stealer at every Python start and start a background loader that could execute code fetched from an attacker-chosen host, though Socket saw its pointer empty at 13:01 UTC. The maintainers' root-cause post of 2026-10-23 says a master key committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked gave the attacker, from 2026-10-10, a GitHub organization owner's CLI token, with which it stole two maintainers' tokens and, on 2026-10-21, overrode branch protection to build the release from a look-alike repository; Socket independently found secret-stealing workflows running on 2026-10-10. Wiz saw stolen AWS instance-role credentials tested about 4.5 hours after exfiltration; PyPI and the registries removed the release the same day and the maintainers say to pin 1.106.2 or an explicit earlier version.
actions: Find every host, build agent and container that installed litellm 1.107.0 from PyPI between 11:39 and 13:23 UTC on 2026-10-21, or pulled the v1.107.0, latest, main-latest or main-stable tag of the official GHCR or Docker Hub LiteLLM images between 11:46 and 14:20 UTC; treat each as compromised, inspect it with tooling that does not start Python in the affected environment, rebuild it from a reviewed artifact pinned to 1.106.2 or an image digest, and rotate every cloud, Kubernetes, registry, SSH, database and AI-provider credential it could read, including the provider keys stored in a LiteLLM proxy database.

last_development.summary: Unit 42's update of 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 names Qilin and Inc as ransomware operators exploiting CVE-2026-0257 and describes one intrusion that pivoted from the VPN gateway to vCenter and ESXi with offline credential theft from a domain controller's virtual disk, so the compromise assessment has to include the virtualization and backup tier.

records.title: CVE-2026-0257, Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect: pre-auth authentication bypass via certificate reuse, marked by CISA as used in ransomware campaigns
records.headline: Qilin and Inc ransomware exploit the GlobalProtect bypass; one intrusion pivoted to vCenter and ESXi past in-guest EDR
records.summary: CVE-2026-0257 is a pre-auth VPN authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CISA KEV; Palo Alto reports limited exploit attempts, and Rapid7 and Unit 42 report successful exploitation): an attacker forges valid auth-override cookies by re-using the GlobalProtect certificate shared with the HTTPS service, with no credentials. CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) marks it as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with this bypass. Unit 42 now names Qilin and Inc as exploiting it and describes one intrusion that pivoted from the VPN gateway to vCenter and ESXi and stole domain credentials offline from a domain controller's virtual disk, which in-guest EDR does not see. Patch or disable auth-override cookies, and treat a gateway that was exposed and unpatched as a compromise-assessment target that includes the virtualization and backup tier.
actions: Patch every PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway to the fixed build in Palo Alto's advisory for its minor release (users then re-authenticate once, because the fixed firewall regenerates the override cookie), or until then disable Authentication Override or give the cookies a certificate that no other feature uses.

On every GlobalProtect gateway that was internet-reachable and unpatched at any time since 2026-05-17, treat the network behind it as a ransomware compromise-assessment target: review VPN sessions that authenticated by cookie from unexpected sources, check Windows hosts for the artifacts Arctic Wolf describes (a ransomware payload staged under C:\\PerfLogs, a PsExec service, an LSASS dump written through comsvcs.dll to an .odt file, an ntdsutil media copy of the Active Directory database, and cleared event logs), and extend the assessment to the virtualization and backup tier: vCenter and ESXi audit logs for a changed execInstalledOnly setting and for access to a domain controller's virtual disk, and the Veeam backup server, because Unit 42 describes one intrusion that pivoted from the gateway to vCenter and dumped domain credentials offline, which in-guest EDR does not see.

records.title: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating
records.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
records.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Confederation headlined its 2026-10-08 release "data outflow confirmed", and the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Tamedia reports that PK Softech had confirmed in writing in January 2026 that it deleted Publica's 2019 migration data, which apparently stayed on its servers, and that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom; Inside IT relays this and adds that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira took data, and Netzwoche relays that the authorities assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left. Publica says personal data of insured persons has presumably left; the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich says its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Pensionskasse Post says personal data left, the Bernische Pensionskasse says it must be assumed so, the Ticino fund IPCT says data of about 1,800 of its insured persons sat on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more, and other funds are still checking. The Federal Data Protection Commissioner, who opened a formal investigation against PK Softech on 2026-10-22, states that data of several pension funds, Publica among them, was exfiltrated. As of 2026-10-22 neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor or the demand.
actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which now says it must be assumed personal data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.

last_update.summary: The 2026-10-25 section said Forescout's 20-plus claimed refrigeration attacks were mostly by Z-Pentest Alliance and NoName057(16); Forescout calls them the most active groups, and the sentence now says so.

last_development.summary: ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, not vulnerabilities researchers had published, so a firmware update alone does not close the exposure. Forescout, on 2026-10-22, counts 12,976 exposed service observations in 99 countries, 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1, and over 20 hacktivist-claimed refrigeration attacks since January 2026, and says the French access vector remains unconfirmed.

records.title: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised, with forced defrost reported at hundreds of French supermarkets; CERT-FR and NCSC Switzerland say to remove internet exposure
records.headline: ANSSI says the refrigeration attacks used exposure and weak passwords, not published flaws; NCSC.ch rates them exploited
records.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, which BFMTV reports as a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of stores. CERT-FR's alert, last revised on 2026-10-16, reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, says campaigns are probably still running and that a factory reset alone does not protect an unpatched end-of-life unit, and in its current text tells owners to check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, and to restart or otherwise factory-reset a compromised Danfoss unit. NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited, and Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October, carried in a Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links, acknowledges a vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers and says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once. Danfoss says most affected units are legacy products or current AK-SM800A units on outdated firmware. ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, rather than vulnerabilities researchers had published; no source names an actor, and the Paris prosecutor is investigating.
actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, against the intended one; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.

last_update.summary: Oracle's second Security Alert of 2026-10-24, CVE-2026-114820 (CVSS 3.1 9.1), removes four root CAs and lists Java SE builds such as 27.0.1.0.2 as affected, and OpenJDK says even a runtime updated in the past few days needs it, so a standalone Java runtime updated on 2026-10-21 needs the new update or the same stop-gap again; OpenJDK now says Debian, Devuan and Ubuntu packages need the keystore recreated by hand. records.title: eMudhra: the private keys of eight intermediate CA certificates were trivially recoverable, so anyone could forge trusted HTTPS certificates; browsers block them, clients with their own trust store or no revocation checking need an update (CVE-2026-111943 in Go)
records.headline: Eight eMudhra CA keys were guessable; Java needs a second update, and Python, Go, Rust and curl stacks need theirs
records.summary: On 2026-10-17 a researcher reported that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates had been generated with too little randomness, so anyone could recover them and forge trusted HTTPS certificates for any site. Firefox, Chrome, Apple and Microsoft platforms block the intermediates and eMudhra revoked them, but software that keeps its own trust store or does not check revocation stays exposed until updated: Go fixed it in 1.27.3 and 1.26.10 as CVE-2026-111943, Python added a built-in denylist as CVE-2026-115557, and Oracle and OpenJDK's Java update of 2026-10-21 (CVE-2026-91403) was followed on 2026-10-24 by a second alert, CVE-2026-114820 (CVSS 3.1 9.1), that removes four root CAs and that OpenJDK says even a runtime updated in the past few days needs. Chrome removes the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root on 2026-10-27; no exploitation is reported.
actions: Update every non-browser TLS client that keeps its own CA bundle or does not check revocation, starting with standalone Java runtimes, including those already updated on 2026-10-21 (Oracle's Security Alert CVE-2026-114820 or the OpenJDK update), pip 26.2.2 or later in every Python environment, Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10, and the CA bundles and base images the incident tracker lists, rebuild container images that embed an older bundle, then confirm with curl against the tracker's test host that the client rejects the certificate.

Replace before 2026-10-27 every TLS certificate your organisation holds that chains to emSign ECC Root CA - G3, by hand where the ACME client does not support ACME Renewal Information, because standard ACME clients do not replace a certificate outside its renewal window.

Apply Cisco's remediation for the products its eMudhra advisory lists as impacted: a TLS policy on Secure Firewall Management Center that blocks the known eMudhra issuers, Duo Access Gateway 3.2.0, Duo Network Gateway 3.4.1, Duo Agentic Authorization Connector 1.0.1 and ThousandEyes Enterprise Agent (Application-hosting Agent 5.2.2) now, and Meraki MV Smart Camera Firmware (2026-11-18), IOS XR 26.4.1 (2026-11-30) and Ultra Cloud Core Subscriber Microservices Infrastructure 2026.04.1 (November 2026) when they ship; other Cisco products are still under investigation.

records.title: Linux kernel ZDI-CAN-33367: a public local root exploit for an skb_zerocopy page-cache write that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with no CVE and no merged fix, among six reports Trend Micro's ZDI copied to public lists, two of them ksmbd flaws scored CVSS 9.0
records.headline: Public root exploit for a Linux page-cache write that gets past the Dirty Frag fix; no CVE and no merged fix yet
records.summary: Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative copied public Linux kernel lists on five kernel reports on 2026-10-21 before any fix was merged, and Sysdig ranks ZDI-CAN-33367 as the one to act on: a local privilege escalation through skb_zerocopy() that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with a public exploit that TuxCare reproduced as root on AlmaLinux 8 to 10, CloudLinux 9 and 10, Debian 12 and 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04. A reviewed patch is on netdev but not merged, none of the six reports has a CVE, and two ksmbd reports that ZDI scores CVSS 9.0 matter only where the in-kernel SMB server runs; no exploitation in the wild is reported.

records.title: NTLM relay past required signing: SpecterOps and Blackfield re-authenticate a signed LDAP or SMB session with a relayed victim identity, and Microsoft fixed it in the September and October 2026 updates
records.headline: Required LDAP and SMB signing did not stop NTLM relay: a re-authenticated session kept the attacker's key
records.summary: SpecterOps (LDAP, 2026-10-23) and Blackfield (SMB, 2026-10-21) independently show that a domain controller or file server that requires signing still accepts a relayed NTLM authentication when the attacker first opens a signed session of its own and then re-authenticates it as the victim, so the session keeps a signing key the attacker knows. Microsoft fixed the SMB variant in September 2026 and the LDAP variant in the 2026-10-13 cumulative update; SpecterOps reports no reply to its report and Blackfield found no CVE for the SMB change; public tooling exists and neither researcher reports use in attacks.
actions: Confirm that every domain controller has the cumulative update of 2026-10-13 and every Windows server the September 2026 one for its Windows release (SpecterOps names KB5126646, the October update for Windows Server 2025, and KB5122882, the September update for Windows Server 2022; other releases have their own packages), then list the computer accounts whose msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity or msDS-KeyCredentialLink holds a value nobody set, because patching does not remove what a relay already wrote.

last_update.summary: Horizon3.ai published a deep dive and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw CVE-2026-106173 on 2026-10-20; the fix and the unexploited status are unchanged.

records.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox GUI authentication bypass (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 9.6) and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 unauthenticated path traversal to code execution (CVE-2026-106173, CVSS 9.4): both critical, fixed 2026-10-13, neither reported exploited
records.headline: FortiSandbox auth bypass (9.6) and FortiSIEM pre-auth RCE (9.4) fixed; FortiSIEM PoC is public, no exploitation listed
records.summary: Fortinet's PSIRT published two critical unauthenticated advisories on 2026-10-13: an authentication bypass in the FortiSandbox GUI (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 3.1 9.6; fixed in 5.0.7 and 4.4.10) and a path traversal in the FortiSIEM phQueryMaster service that allows code execution (CVE-2026-106173, 9.4; FortiSIEM 7.5.0 only, fixed in 7.5.1, workaround: restrict tcp port 27918). Fortinet lists neither as known to be exploited, and Horizon3.ai published a write-up and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw on 2026-10-20. The FortiSandbox ranges include 5.0.6 and 4.4.9, the builds that fixed CVE-2026-25089, one of three FortiSandbox flaws reported exploited in June, so a unit patched for that one is still affected.
actions: Check every FortiSandbox that was upgraded to 5.0.6 or 4.4.9 after the exploited-flaw advisories of this year: those builds are still affected by CVE-2026-107656 and need 5.0.7 or 4.4.10; on FortiSIEM 7.5.0 install 7.5.1, or until then restrict access to tcp 27918 as Fortinet's workaround says.

records.title: CVE-2026-110264, GitLab CE/EE: an unauthenticated code-execution flaw in the Org-mode renderer's regular-expression handling, fixed in 19.5.1, 19.4.3 and 19.3.6 and backported to four older lines (CVSS 10.0)
records.headline: GitLab's critical patch fixes an unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 RCE in Org-mode rendering; no exploitation reported
records.summary: GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-21 fixes CVE-2026-110264 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in regular-expression handling that lets an unauthenticated user run code on a self-managed GitLab server as the git user; GitLab's own detection write-ups place it in the rendering of .org files, which needs only a public project that can hold the payload. Every version from 7.0 before 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, 19.2.9, 19.3.6, 19.4.3 and 19.5.1 is affected, so instances on the 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8 builds that closed the earlier regular-expression flaws still need this release. The bug sits in Ruby's own regular-expression engine, which Ruby fixed on 2026-10-23 in 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13, so any Ruby application that compiles attacker-controlled patterns is exposed to it. GitLab does not report exploitation.
actions: Upgrade every self-managed GitLab CE and EE instance to 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6 or the backport for its line (19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10, 18.11.13) now, internet-reachable instances and instances with public projects first; builds 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8 are still affected.

records.title: MythicRatatoskr: ESET documents a Go backdoor that hides its command server inside the Yggdrasil mesh network, and a UAC-0099 to Sandworm access handoff that ended in a Group Policy wiper attack on a Ukrainian grain logistics firm
records.headline: ESET: a backdoor reaches its C2 through the Yggdrasil mesh; Sandworm wiped the victim two months after UAC-0099 got in
records.summary: ESET reports that UAC-0099 gained access to a Ukrainian grain logistics company on 2025-07-16 with a spearphishing attachment and a day later deployed MythicRatatoskr, a Go backdoor whose command server sits inside the Yggdrasil mesh network, reached through public peers; on 2025-09-17 the SDelete utility was deployed through Group Policy, which ESET assesses with high confidence as Sandworm after UAC-0099 handed off the access. ESET names blocking the public peer addresses as a viable mitigation.

last_update.summary: The CVE-2022-21894 record attributed its mitigation to Microsoft's KB5025885, which documents the revocation for CVE-2023-24932; the record now rests on Kaspersky's statement that the Baton Drop patch revokes the Windows Production PCA 2011 certificate and must be triggered manually.

records.title: BlackX: Kaspersky finds a BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit on fully patched Windows machines of Central Asian diplomatic bodies, because the Baton Drop fix does not revoke the old boot-manager certificate until an administrator triggers it
records.headline: Kaspersky: a UEFI bootkit ran on fully patched Windows because Microsoft's Secure Boot revocation is off by default
records.summary: Kaspersky GReAT reports BlackX, a UEFI bootkit similar to BlackLotus that exploits Baton Drop (CVE-2022-21894) to enrol attacker keys and load a kernel driver that blinds security products, installed after attackers held administrator rights on networks of diplomatic agencies in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan; Kaspersky attributes it to APT41 with medium confidence. The targeted machines were fully patched, because Microsoft's fix revokes the old boot-manager certificate only when an administrator sets a registry flag and runs a scheduled task.

records.title: M365 token spray and replay: Huntress tracks a 10-week campaign that replays stolen post-MFA tokens from rented hosting within minutes, registers rogue Entra devices, wipes and re-registers MFA methods and hides mail with inbox rules of one to three characters or punctuation only
records.headline: Huntress: stolen post-MFA M365 tokens replayed within minutes; a password reset leaves planted devices and MFA methods
records.summary: Huntress reports that between 2026-07-14 and 2026-09-22 it detected 497 Microsoft 365 sign-in events in 79 organizations that replayed tokens stolen through adversary-in-the-middle relays, device-code phishing and social engineering, within minutes of capture and from one rented hosting range. The operators then registered rogue Entra devices, wiped and replaced MFA methods in 19 organizations and hid mail with inbox rules; a password reset alone removes none of it.
actions: In every Entra tenant, list the devices registered since 2026-07-14 whose names are DESKTOP- followed by eight uppercase hexadecimal characters, the authenticators that were deleted and re-registered within minutes, and the inbox rules whose names are one to three characters or punctuation only or that move mail to RSS Feeds, RSS Subscriptions or Conversation History, and remove what nobody created; then revoke the sessions of any affected user, because a password reset leaves the devices, MFA methods and a roughly 90-minute access token in place.

records.title: Fortinet coordinated security hardening release: critical and high-severity fixes in FortiOS 8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.13 and 7.2.14, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, with the advisories withheld until 2026-11-10
records.headline: Fortinet ships out-of-cycle critical and high fixes for FortiOS and four more products; CVEs wait until 10 November
records.summary: Fortinet announced on 2026-10-21 a coordinated release of critical and high-severity fixes for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (scheduled for 2026-10-22, after recent FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator releases), found through its AI-assisted testing, and urges every customer to upgrade at once, internet-facing devices first. The CVE advisories follow only on 2026-11-10, so there are no identifiers to triage by; NCSC.ch lists the exploitation status as unknown, and the FortiMail builds are the ones that already fix CVE-2026-104286, which Fortinet reports as exploited.
actions: Upgrade every internet-facing FortiOS (8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.13 or 7.2.14), FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (8.0.2, 7.6.8, 7.4.12 or 7.2.13), FortiMail (8.0.2, 7.6.7 or 7.4.9; 7.2 moves to 7.4 or later) and FortiAuthenticator (8.0.4 or 6.6.11) now rather than in the November cycle, saving the configuration first; where the upgrade has to wait, restrict HTTPS and SSH administration to trusted addresses or disable it on external interfaces and keep FortiManager administration off the internet.

records.title: CVE-2026-114625, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem: an SQL injection lets any authenticated user, down to the Enterprise Read Only role, act as a superuser operator, and Arista says it is actively exploited (CVSS 3.1 9.9)
records.headline: Arista confirms exploitation of a VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw: any tenant login, even read-only, reaches operator rights
records.summary: Arista's Security Advisory 0199 of 2026-10-22 fixes CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 3.1 9.9) in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator: any authenticated user, down to the lowest built-in tenant role, can gain operator privileges and reach functions meant for internal use only, and Arista says the flaw is known to be actively exploited. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; hosted and dedicated Orchestrators were already patched, and Arista names no actor, victim count or start date.
actions: Upgrade every on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator to 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 or 6.4.2.12 (or later in its train) now and, until then, restrict its web interface to trusted administrative networks; before upgrading, preserve the web access, application, system and database logs and the file-system timestamps, then check the host for backdoor daemons, web shells and unexpected outbound traffic.

records.headline: OVHcloud CLI release binaries carried a secret-stealing build for about 90 minutes; a pinned hash caught it
records.summary: OVHcloud says a hacker used a developer's GitHub account to replace the release binaries of its command-line tool for versions v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 on 2026-10-19 with a build that steals secrets from disk, available for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times; the first replacement was at about 12:47 UTC and OVHcloud deleted the files at 14:21 UTC after a customer's pinned SHA-256 failed. Its postmortem traces the account compromise to a poisoned editor extension installed on the developer's personal MacBook on 2025-10-20, ties it to the GlassWorm actor through a Solana wallet, and names a missing release-immutability setting as the main issue. Anyone who installed or updated the tool from a release asset in that window must rotate every secret on that host; the source tag and the Go module were untouched.
actions: Find every workstation, build agent and container image build that installed or updated the OVHcloud CLI from a release asset (install script, Homebrew cask, direct download or a CI step fetching the release tarball) between 12:47 and 14:21 UTC on 2026-10-19, and rotate every secret readable on each of those hosts before installing v0.16.0 or later.

records.title: k0t: Group-IB and NyxLab describe a probable access broker that mass-exploits FortiWeb and PAN-OS GlobalProtect, brute-forces FortiGate and decrypts stolen FortiGate configurations offline with the default key, with victims later listed by Qilin and The Gentlemen
records.headline: Group-IB: k0t takes edge devices in bulk and decrypts FortiGate configurations offline; enable private-data-encryption
records.summary: Group-IB and NyxLab report a campaign by an operator they track as k0t that finds exposed FortiGate, FortiWeb and PAN-OS GlobalProtect devices in bulk, exploits FortiWeb CVE-2025-64446 and GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 or brute-forces FortiGate logins, downloads each FortiGate configuration and decrypts its stored LDAP, Active Directory and administrator secrets offline with the default FortiOS key, which cannot be seen on the appliance. Group-IB then sees hands-on Active Directory work, remote-management persistence and exfiltration, and victims that later appear on the Qilin and The Gentlemen leak sites; it assesses the operators as probable initial-access brokers but says the link to either group is unconfirmed.
actions: On every FortiGate (FortiOS 5.6.11, 6.0.7, 6.2.1 or later; check the FortiManager and HA note in Fortinet's FG-IR-19-007 first where it applies), enable private-data-encryption with an operator-defined key, and for any device that was internet-reachable with a brute-forceable administrator login or an unpatched exposed service, treat the LDAP and Active Directory bind and administrator credentials stored in its configuration as known to the attacker and rotate them, bind accounts first.

records.title: CVE-2026-76466, Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E: unauthenticated root command execution on clustered devices, fixed in X15.5.20 with no workaround (CVSS 9.8), alongside same-day hardening releases for Unified CM, Unity Connection and Snort 3
records.headline: Cisco: unauthenticated root RCE on clustered Expressway, fixed only in X15.5.20; X14 and earlier must migrate
records.summary: Cisco's disclosure of 2026-10-21 fixes CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 3.1 9.8), which lets an unauthenticated attacker who holds persistent cookies run operating-system commands as root on Expressway-C and Expressway-E that are configured in a cluster; X15.5.3 and earlier get X15.5.20, X14 and earlier must migrate, and there is no workaround. Hardening releases ship the same day for the Unified CM family and Unity Connection (up to 9.8, fixed in 15SU5), and for Snort 3 in Secure Firewall Threat Defense and related products (9.0); Cisco knows of no malicious use of any of them.
actions: On every Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E, upgrade to X15.5.20, clustered units first because only they carry the unauthenticated root flaw, and plan the migration of any unit still on X14 or earlier, which has no fix and no workaround.

records.headline: Leaked BitLocker bypass "YellowKey" and CTFMON privilege escalation "GreenPlasma" were fixed in the June 2026 updates
records.summary: Nightmare Eclipse published exploit code in May 2026 for YellowKey (CVE-2026-45585), a physical-access BitLocker bypass through the Windows Recovery Environment that defeats TPM-only configurations, and GreenPlasma (CVE-2026-45586), a CTFMON elevation of privilege to SYSTEM. Microsoft fixed both in the June 2026 Windows updates of 2026-06-09 and marks neither as exploited. Microsoft says TPM+PIN blocks YellowKey, which the researcher disputes.

last_update.summary: The account of Microsoft's 2026-10-15 notice now cites what each page carries: the release post records the banner and its replacement on 2026-10-16 by a link to a dedicated post, which names the Windows updates and the OWA and mail-queue symptoms. The banner's statement that Microsoft was investigating with its Windows partners no longer appears on any page and is dropped.

last_development.summary: Microsoft's Exchange Team now gives a workaround for the instability that the October 2026 Windows Server updates can cause on Exchange servers: it advises against uninstalling them and says setting the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap to 65536 and rebooting has solved the cases it assisted. It adds that DAG members losing quorum are among the reported symptoms and that the Exchange security updates are not the cause.

records.title: CVE-2026-70571, Microsoft Exchange Server: an unauthenticated crafted-email code-execution flaw in the October 2026 security updates, the last Exchange 2016 and 2019 updates under the paid ESU (CVSS 8.1)
records.headline: Exchange October updates fix an unauthenticated email-borne RCE; 2016 and 2019 get their last update, and only with ESU
records.summary: Microsoft's 2026-10-13 Exchange security updates fix CVE-2026-70571, a stack-based buffer overflow that an unauthenticated attacker can trigger with a crafted email (Critical, CVSS 8.1 with high attack complexity, Exploitation More Likely, not exploited), and CVE-2026-70279, a 9.3 cross-site scripting flaw that lets an attacker act as an administrator who clicks a crafted link. October is the last month Exchange 2016 and 2019 customers enrolled in the Period 2 ESU receive newly released updates, and organisations without ESU have no 2016 or 2019 update at all. Microsoft's Exchange Team says the October Windows Server updates (KB5126646, KB5126655, KB5126651, KB5126868) can make Exchange servers unstable, with OWA failures, growing mail queues and lost DAG quorum, whether or not the Exchange update is installed; it advises against uninstalling them and on 2026-10-17 gave a registry workaround.
actions: Install the October 2026 Exchange security update on every Exchange server and on every machine that has the Exchange Management Tools; on Exchange 2016 and 2019 servers that are not covered by the Period 2 ESU, decide now between enrolling (it only gets an organisation current through this release) and moving to Exchange Subscription Edition, because after October Microsoft ships updates for Subscription Edition only.

On every Exchange server that has the October 2026 Windows Server update installed, do not uninstall it; where OWA fails with MapiExceptionMdbOffline, mail queues grow or a DAG member cannot reach quorum, set the registry value EpmapSavedContextCap (REG_DWORD) under HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Rpc to 65536, reboot, and raise the limit if the failure recurs.

last_update.summary: The status of build 25.1.3.0 now rests on Ivanti's own description of the flaw, which covers versions before 25.1.3.0, beside Rapid7's table and CERT-FR's alert, which counts 25.1.3.0 as affected; 25.1.3.1 stays the target build.

last_development.summary: CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance, and sets the response order: isolate the appliance from the internet and the internal network, snapshot and keep it powered on, then analyse before any reset; its rotation scope also covers Kerberos tickets of the service accounts and licence-server authentication. CERT-FR also counts 25.1.3.0 as affected, so the fixed-build targets now name 25.1.3.1.

records.title: CVE-2026-104935, Ivanti Connect Secure: an authentication bypass chained to code execution is exploited as a zero-day, and the root-escalation step of the chain was unpatched at disclosure (CVSS 8.6)
records.headline: Exploited Ivanti Connect Secure chain: its root step had no fix at disclosure, and it evades the Integrity Checker
records.summary: Ivanti disclosed CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13, an authentication bypass in Connect Secure that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker run commands, and says it is aware of limited exploitation; CISA listed it in KEV the same day. Volexity found a cluster it calls UTA0576 chaining it with a root escalation that Ivanti had not fixed when Volexity reported (a separate record, CVE-2026-111357, now covers that step), patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. Fixed builds are 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.5 (Ivanti's own description of the flaw and Rapid7 place 25.1.3.0 outside the affected range, while CERT-FR counts it as affected); a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and CERT-FR says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance and tells owners to isolate and preserve it before any reset.
actions: Upgrade every Ivanti Connect Secure appliance on 25.1.1.1 or earlier, 25.1.2.2 or earlier, or 22.8R2.4 or earlier to 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.5 now, internet-facing appliances first; 22.7.x and below are not affected.

Run a compromise check on every appliance that was reachable on an affected build, starting with proxy, load balancer or WAF logs back to at least 2026-10-03 for welcome.cgi requests that carry an X-DSCGI-PATH header; where compromise cannot be excluded, first cut the appliance off from the internet and the internal network and snapshot a virtual appliance's file system and memory without powering it down, then follow Ivanti's recovery steps and reset the domain service account, LAPS and local passwords, certificates, API keys, the Kerberos tickets of its service accounts and the licence-server authentication the appliance held, because CERT-FR knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets.

last_update.summary: Adds a compromise check: watchTowr says Citrix provides an indicator-of-compromise script for exposed appliances, though a clean result is not definitive proof. Citrix's own pages for this flaw describe no such check.

last_development.summary: Rapid7's incident analysis shows CVE-2026-88779 used as the crash and reboot trigger of a root-execution chain with CVE-2026-88771 on an affected 14.1 NetScaler, with the call-home crash handler running the attacker's payload as root after the reboot; repeated crashes on an appliance not yet patched for CVE-2026-88771 now call for a compromise check.

records.title: CVE-2026-88779, Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: a SAML-triggered memory overflow still hits appliances on the September fixed builds, and Citrix confirms targeted attacks (CVSS 4.0 8.7)
records.headline: Citrix confirms attacks on a new NetScaler SAML flaw that the September fixed builds do not close
records.summary: Citrix's bulletin CTX697174 fixes CVE-2026-88779, a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that a network attacker needing no privileges reaches when the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider; Citrix says it has observed targeted attacks and scopes the impact to denial of service. Appliances already on the 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 builds that fixed the September zero-days remain affected and must move to 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28 or the FIPS builds, and identity-provider appliances then need 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29 or the FIPS builds, which close the further SAML flaw CVE-2026-107406 that Citrix disclosed on 2026-10-08. Reports of code execution on patched honeypots are unconfirmed, and CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 2026-10-04. Rapid7's incident analysis of 2026-10-19 shows the crash used as the reboot trigger of a root-execution chain with CVE-2026-88771 on an affected 14.1 appliance, so repeated crashes on an appliance not yet patched for that flaw call for a compromise check.
actions: Upgrade every SAML-configured NetScaler (`add authentication samlAction` or `add authentication samlIdPProfile`) that is still below 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28, 14.1-73.41 FIPS or 13.1-37.282, including appliances on the 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 builds, to at least those builds; identity providers then need the builds named for CVE-2026-107406. Where the upgrade has to wait and NetScaler Console virtual patching is available, confirm with `show appfw signatures` that the Global Deny List signature version is at least v24, which Citrix offers as a bridge for CVE-2026-88779 only.

Before restarting a SAML-configured NetScaler that has crashed or rebooted repeatedly, preserve its logs and crash artifacts, open a Citrix support case, which Citrix asks for when an appliance is experiencing the impact, and search its authentication logs for shell metacharacters next to Pitboss crash-message text, because Rapid7 saw a crash-and-reboot cycle used to make the call-home crash handler run an attacker's payload as root.

records.title: APT28 (Swallowtail) used the HOOKEDGE backdoor against a law-enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder and an aircraft-engine maker in two NATO states; at the shipbuilder it then pushed an SSH key for a persistent tunnel, captured NTLM handshakes and ran a reflective loader
records.headline: Symantec: APT28's hidden-Edge backdoor hit law-enforcement and defence targets; at a shipbuilder it added an SSH tunnel
records.summary: Symantec reports that APT28, which it tracks as Swallowtail, used the HOOKEDGE backdoor against a law-enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder and a military aircraft-engine manufacturer in two NATO member states, none named. A macro-enabled Word document started a script chain that uses a hidden, off-screen Microsoft Edge window as its HTTP client against a public webhook service; at the shipbuilder the operators then pushed an SSH private key for a persistent tunnel, captured NTLM handshakes from the host itself and ran a previously undocumented in-memory loader, in an intrusion that lasted at least two months. Recorded Future had documented HOOKEDGE against government and diplomatic targets in Romania, Spain and Turkiye in August.

records.title: AA26-293A: FBI, CISA and German and UK law enforcement describe SafePay ransomware, which enters through VPN credentials and five edge-device and backup-server flaws and factory-resets backup NAS devices before encrypting
records.headline: Joint advisory on SafePay: VPN credentials and five old edge and backup flaws in, backup NAS wiped before encryption
records.summary: CISA, the FBI, the US Secret Service, Germany's LKA Rheinland-Pfalz and UK law enforcement published advisory AA26-293A on 2026-10-20 on SafePay, which they say was among the most active ransomware groups in 2026 and has affected at least 600 victims, in Europe among other regions. Access comes from exposed credentials, brute force and phished account profiles used over Mullvad VPN addresses, and from five known flaws in Cisco ASA and Firepower Threat Defense, Veeam Backup and Replication and SonicWall SonicOS; the distinctive step is stopping the Volume Shadow Copy Service and factory-resetting the network storage that holds backups before encryption.
